claim: For every positive integer \(n\), the congruence \(T_aT_b+n\equiv c^2\pmod M\), with \(T_j=j(j+1)/2\), has integer solutions \((a,b,c)\) for every positive modulus \(M\) if and only if \(n\not\equiv2,5\pmod 9\).

correctness.rationale: Necessity follows from the exact modulo-3 and modulo-9 residue argument. Sufficiency is proved prime-power by prime-power: triangular residues are bijective modulo powers of 2 on a complete index range; the odd-prime transformed conic has a nonsingular finite-field point for every p>3; and the three admissible 3-adic cases have explicit simple Hensel seeds. CRT then combines the local solutions. The finite verifier checks representative identities and residue patterns but is not used as an infinite proof.
